skills.name: Law of sines
skills.wrong_turn: Match each side with the angle across from it. Side a pairs with angle A on the far side, not with an angle at one of its ends.

skills.name: Ambiguous case
skills.wrong_turn: When sin B gives an acute B, don't stop. Check whether 180° − B also fits: with SSA there may be two triangles.
skills.rule: SSA with acute A: compare a with the height h=bsinA.

skills.name: Law of cosines
skills.wrong_turn: Multiply before subtracting. In c² = 49 + 64 − 112 cos C, don't compute (113 − 112) cos C.

skills.name: Choosing the law
skills.wrong_turn: The law of sines can't start an SAS or SSS problem. There is no side with its opposite angle known yet.
skills.rule: SAS or SSS: law of cosines. AAS or ASA: law of sines. SSA: law of sines, carefully.

skills.name: Solve any triangle
skills.wrong_turn: Don't force a triangle that can't exist. 3, 4, 8 fails 3 + 4 > 8, and the law of cosines gives cos C = −1.625, which is impossible.
skills.rule: Find the first missing part with the right law, the next angle by the angle sum, the last side by sines.

skills.name: Area with sine

steps.c: find a missing side from area

skills.wrong_turn: The angle must be between the two sides you use. With sides a and b, use angle C, not A or B.

skills.name: Heron's formula
skills.wrong_turn: s is half the perimeter, not the whole perimeter. For 13, 14, 15, s = 21, not 42.

skills.name: Bearings & navigation
skills.wrong_turn: Bearings go clockwise from north, not counterclockwise from east like math angles. Bearing 030° is the math angle 60°.
skills.rule: A bearing is the clockwise angle from north, written with three digits: 045°, 210°.

skills.name: Surveying problems
skills.wrong_turn: The angle at the far point is 180° − A − B, not one you measured. It sits opposite the baseline in the law of sines.
skills.rule: Measure a baseline and the two angles at its ends; then use the law of sines.
